Summary — Base Account / Basenames documentation (LLM-friendly, concise)

OVERVIEW — main features & capabilities
- Base Account = smart-wallet (ERC‑4337) + SDK that enables: universal sign-in (Sign in with Base / SIWE), one-tap USDC payments (Base Pay), gasless/sponsored transactions (paymasters), batch/atomic transactions, sub-accounts (app-specific child wallets), spend permissions (signed EIP‑712 allowances), profile data collection (dataCallback), and Basenames (onchain human-readable names like alice.base.eth).
- SDK provides an EIP‑1193 provider and utility helpers for key management, sub-account management, pay APIs, and capabilities detection.
- Integrations: Wagmi/viem, OnchainKit, Privy, Mobile Wallet Protocol, plain web/React/React Native examples and prebuilt UI components (SignInWithBaseButton, BasePayButton).

CORE CONCEPTS & ARCHITECTURE (short)
- SDK (createBaseAccountSDK): returns BaseAccountSDK with getProvider() (EIP‑1193 provider) + subAccount manager.
- Wallet Service: passkey + session key flows; popup or mobile deep-link handles user approval.
- Smart Wallet contracts: ERC‑4337 accounts on supported chains. ERC‑6492 wrapper allows signature verification before deployment.
- Capabilities: chain/account-specific feature flags (atomic, auxiliaryFunds/MagicSpend, paymasterService, datacallback, flowControl, signInWithEthereum). Query via wallet_getCapabilities.
- Provider request handling: some calls are handled locally by SDK, some sent to wallet UI, others forwarded to RPC provider.

KEY SDK / API METHODS (purpose)
- createBaseAccountSDK(options) — initialize SDK (appName, appLogoUrl, appChainIds, preference.attribution, telemetry, subAccounts.toOwnerAccount, paymasterUrls).
- sdk.getProvider() — EIP‑1193 provider for RPC requests and events (accountsChanged, chainChanged).
- pay(params) — send USDC payment (amount, to, testnet?, payerInfo for data collection). Returns { id }.
- getPaymentStatus({id, testnet}) — poll payment status: completed/pending/failed/not_found.
- requestSpendPermission(params) — build & request user EIP‑712 signed spend permission.
- fetchPermissions({account, chainId, spender, provider}) — list active permissions.
- getPermissionStatus(permission) — remainingSpend, isActive, nextPeriodStart.
- prepareSpendCallData({permission, amount}) — returns call(s) (approveWithSignature optional + spend) for spender to submit.
- requestRevoke(permission) — prompts user to revoke permission (onchain).
- prepareRevokeCallData(permission) — silent revoke calldata for spender to submit.
- generateKeyPair() / getKeypair() — P256 key pair creation / retrieval for sub-accounts.
- getCryptoKeyAccount() — returns current crypto key account (WebAuthn/local) or null.
- sdk.subAccount.* — sub-account create/get/addOwner/setToOwnerAccount helpers.

IMPORTANT PROVIDER RPC METHODS (what to call & why)
- wallet_connect(options) — connect + request capabilities (use for SIWE: signInWithEthereum {nonce, chainId}).
- wallet_sendCalls(params) — send batch of calls (version "2.0.0"), supports atomicRequired, capabilities (paymasterService, dataCallback, etc.). Use for batching approve+transfer, sponsored transactions, or multi-step flows.
- wallet_getCallsStatus(callsId) — poll batch status & receipts.
- wallet_getCapabilities(account) — detect per-chain capabilities (atomic, paymasterService, auxiliaryFunds, datacallback, flowControl).
- wallet_addSubAccount / wallet_getSubAccounts — create or fetch sub accounts.
- eth_requestAccounts / eth_accounts — standard connect / get authorized addresses.
- eth_sendTransaction / eth_sendRawTransaction — send transactions when needed.
- eth_signTypedData_v4 / personal_sign — typed data and personal signatures (EIP‑712, EIP‑191).
- wallet_addEthereumChain / wallet_switchEthereumChain / wallet_watchAsset — network & token management helpers.
- coinbase_fetchPermissions — Coinbase-specific fetch for spend permissions.

ESSENTIAL USAGE PATTERNS & SHORT EXAMPLES

1) Sign-in with Base (SIWE using wallet_connect)
- Generate nonce (crypto.randomUUID()).
- Call wallet_connect with capability signInWithEthereum: { nonce, chainId: '0x2105' }.
- Receive accounts[0].capabilities.signInWithEthereum => { message, signature }.
- Verify signature on backend (viem.verifyMessage / verifyTypedData), create session.

Example flow (pseudocode):
- nonce = fresh
- provider.request({ method: 'wallet_connect', params: [{ version:'1', capabilities: { signInWithEthereum: {nonce, chainId} } }] })
- send { address, message, signature } to backend -> verify -> issue session

2) One-tap payments (pay + getPaymentStatus)
- Client: pay({ amount: "5.00", to: "0xRecipient", testnet: true, payerInfo?: {...} })
- Save returned payment.id; poll getPaymentStatus({id, testnet}) until status === "completed".
- Optional: include payerInfo.requests and callbackURL for server validation (HTTPS required).

3) Batch / atomic transactions (wallet_sendCalls)
- Build calls array (to, value, data).
- Check wallet_getCapabilities(account) to see if atomic supported.
- provider.request({ method: 'wallet_sendCalls', params: [{ version:'2.0.0', from, chainId, atomicRequired:true, calls, capabilities: { paymasterService: { url } } }] })

4) Sub Accounts (improve UX, avoid passkey every action)
- Use provider.wallet_getSubAccounts to fetch or wallet_addSubAccount to create.
- Configure SDK or Privy to use embedded wallet as owner (toOwnerAccount) so Sub Account operations are signed by embedded wallet without passkey.
- Use sub-account address as `from` for eth_sendTransaction or wallet_sendCalls.

5) Spend Permissions (allow spender to spend without repeated user prompts)
- requestSpendPermission(...) — user signs EIP‑712 permission.
- prepareSpendCallData(permission, amount) — returns calls array (maybe approveWithSignature + spend).
- Submit spendCalls from spender account via wallet_sendCalls or eth_sendTransaction(s).
- Revoke via requestRevoke (user popup) or prepareRevokeCallData (silent, for spender account).

6) Data collection during payment (dataCallback)
- Add capabilities.dataCallback in wallet_sendCalls or pay().
- Provide callbackURL (HTTPS) that will receive requestedInfo. Validate and return either { request: { calls, chainId, capabilities } } to proceed, or { errors: {...} } to prompt user corrections.

CONFIGURATION OPTIONS — createBaseAccountSDK (key fields)
- appName (string) — required-ish for UI.
- appLogoUrl (string)
- appChainIds (number[]) — which chains app supports.
- preference:
  - attribution: { auto: boolean } or dataSuffix hex
  - telemetry: boolean (default true; can disable)
- subAccounts: { toOwnerAccount: async () => ({ account: LocalAccount | WebAuthnAccount | null }) } — required to sign sub-account operations.
- paymasterUrls: { [chainId]: url } — default paymaster endpoints / proxies.

INTEGRATIONS & CONFIG SNIPPETS (brief)
- Wagmi: createConfig({ chains:[base], connectors: [ baseAccount({...}) ], transports: { [base.id]: http() } }) and use connector.provider to call Base Account RPCs.
- OnchainKit: use <Identity/> to resolve Basenames; use resolver ABI + viem to read resolver records.
- Privy: configure embeddedWallets, include base_account in walletList and use usePrivy / useWallets hooks to get wallets and baseAccountSdk.

BASENAMES (naming system)
- Basenames = ENS-based human-readable names on Base; fully onchain.
- Registration: fees vary by length; discounts/free for specific users or NFTs; initial launch may include a Dutch auction premium.
- Transfer process: use Base.org names UI -> Transfer name -> paste new address -> sign four transactions in order (transfer token ownership, transfer management, change address resolution, send NFT). New owner must set as primary to activate.
- Integration: resolve names using L2Resolver ABI (viem), use namehash / reverse node conversion (OnchainKit provides helper convertReverseNodeToBytes).

IMPORTANT WARNINGS & BEST PRACTICES
- Always verify SIWE signatures server-side; use fresh, unique nonces and track them to prevent replay.
- popup blockers & COOP: ensure wallet popups are triggered directly by clicks and use Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy that allows popups (same-origin-allow-popups or unsafe-none).
- For Basename transfers: use Basenames UI; marketplace transfers (OpenSea) only move NFT, not resolver/management.
- dataCallback: callback URL must be HTTPS (ngrok allowed for dev); must return the request object or errors per spec.
- MagicSpend (auxiliaryFunds): if capability present, do not block UX based on onchain balance alone.
- Check wallet_getCapabilities before using optional features (atomic, paymasterService, auxiliaryFunds, datacallback, flowControl).
- Telemetry is opt-out via SDK option telemetry:false.

ERRORS & CODES (common)
- wallet_sendCalls error codes: 4001 user rejected, 5700 missing capability required, 5740 batch too large, 5720 duplicate batch id, 5750 EIP-7702 upgrade rejected.
- Standard provider errors: 4001 user rejected, 4100 method not supported, -32602 invalid params.

TYPICAL DEV WORKFLOW (quick)
1. createBaseAccountSDK({ appName, appChainIds, ... })
2. provider = sdk.getProvider()
3. Detect capabilities: provider.request({ method:'wallet_getCapabilities', params:[account] })
4. For SIWE: provider.request({ method:'wallet_connect', params:[{capabilities:{signInWithEthereum:{nonce,chainId}}}] })
5. For payments: use pay() helper or wallet_sendCalls + paymaster capability
6. For batched contract flows: build calls => wallet_sendCalls(...); poll wallet_getCallsStatus(callsId)
7. For SubAccounts/SpendPermissions: use sdk.subAccount & spend-permission utilities (requestSpendPermission, prepareSpendCallData, fetchPermissions)

WHERE TO LOOK (reference)
- Provider RPC methods: wallet_connect, wallet_sendCalls, wallet_getCapabilities, wallet_getCallsStatus, etc.
- Spend permission utilities: requestSpendPermission, prepareSpendCallData, requestRevoke, prepareRevokeCallData, fetchPermissions, getPermissionStatus.
- Pay API: pay, getPaymentStatus.
- UI components: SignInWithBaseButton, BasePayButton in @base-org/account-ui/react.
- Basenames: resolver ABI, resolver read flows, transfer steps.
